suggestions.rationale: Recent systematic-review and meta-analytic evidence supports an association between chronic rhinosinusitis and obstructive sleep apnea, including a modest higher OSA risk among CRS patients. Although Mendelian-randomization results in the same study support a directional CRS-to-OSA signal, this repository does not translate population-level or genetic evidence into an automatic individual causal nexus. The relationship remains association-focused and requires confirmed CRS and OSA diagnoses, chronology, sinonasal phenotype/severity, body-habitus and upper-airway factors, medication context, and competing OSA causes.
evidenceGaps: ENT documentation confirming chronic rhinosinusitis phenotype, duration, objective findings, and severity
Polysomnography or validated sleep-study documentation confirming OSA and severity
CRS and OSA chronology, including whether OSA findings changed with effective sinonasal treatment
BMI/weight trajectory, craniofacial or upper-airway factors, age, sedating medications, and other OSA risk factors
ENT/sleep specialist assessment distinguishing population-level association from the individual's causal or aggravation theory

sourceReferences.citation: Zhai JH, Zhu LL, Chen SQ, Jian X, Chen C. Association between chronic rhinosinusitis and obstructive sleep apnea: evidence from systematic review, meta-analysis, and Mendelian Randomization. Sleep Biol Rhythms. 2026;24(2):183-194. PMID 41969980
sourceReferences.note: Systematic review/meta-analysis of 14 observational studies (30,509 participants) found 20% OSA prevalence among CRS patients and modestly elevated OSA risk (OR 1.14, 95% CI 1.08-1.20); MR supported a CRS-to-OSA directional signal. Repository wording remains association-focused for individual claim research.
